prompt: Eye-level view standing in a narrow, steep cobblestone lane in the old town of Veliko Tarnovo, Bulgaria (Varusha quarter), looking uphill. Bulgarian National Revival houses line both sides: rough grey-beige stone ground floors with heavy dark wooden doors, whitewashed and warm ochre plaster upper floors projecting over the street on dark wooden brackets, small wooden-framed windows with green and brown shutters, red geraniums in window boxes, wide eaves with curved terracotta roof tiles, wrought-iron wall lanterns. The lane curves gently uphill to the left. On the right, a gap between houses with a low stone parapet opens to a view across the gorge to Tsarevets hill with medieval stone fortress walls and the Patriarchal church with its bell tower. Autumn afternoon, warm low sun from the left, long shadows across the cobbles, scattered fallen yellow leaves, a red vintage scooter parked by a wall. No people, no cars, no text. Clear spatial depth, coherent architecture, rich detail, stylized painterly look.
